title: The transfer's completion report, and what it will not have proved
description: GitHub #44. `a5` reports when the 46.3 GB copy finishes: counts, every failure individually, and **real tests** — a file played there, a page loaded, `MediaItem::count()` against 8,315. Also what remains unverified, because a finished transfer will imply more than it proved: **part 2 of #37** (placing a complete `.part`) is unexercised precisely because part 1 prevents the condition, and the progress endpoint on this machine is migrated and live, but no report has arrived yet (`progress_at: never`), so the payload is still unconfirmed end to end. Three things to check that would otherwise be missed: the skipped rows are the ones we know about — 3 at last count, not the 6 measured before a hand reset; **profiles were not transferred** (S-73 — the request was `metadata,files`); and the 7 corrupt titles from #39 may simply be gone, since after the copy those rows are the Mac's, which are clean. S-95 becomes runnable for the first time — `a5` will hold all 9,737 files rather than 918

title: Dual licensing (AGPLv3 + commercial)
description: SoundChex is now dual-licensed: AGPLv3 (default, free) **or** a commercial licence from Tripsittr LLC for those who can't/won't comply with the AGPL (closed-source embedding, hosting without publishing modifications). Scaffold added: `LICENSING.md` (explainer + which-do-I-need table), `CLA.md` (contributor licence agreement — the load-bearing piece: it keeps the relicensing right so the project *can* be dual-licensed; without it, an outside contribution can't go into the commercial licence), `COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.md` (draft shape of the agreement), README updated, contact `licensing@soundchex.app`. **Prerequisite that must hold:** Tripsittr LLC must own/have relicensing rights to all first-party code — true today (essentially all owner's code); the CLA protects it going forward. Third-party deps are NOT relicensed (they keep their permissive licences — S-155 audit). A full **commercial licence agreement draft** now exists at `legal/COMMERCIAL-LICENSE-AGREEMENT.md` (Arizona/Phoenix jurisdiction filled; fees/term/scope bracketed) — a working document to bring to counsel. **Still to do (human/legal):** counsel review + finalisation of that draft, a CLA-enforcement mechanism (bot/checkbox), the `licensing@` inbox, and website positioning (a public licensing page). All legal wording is draft-pending-review.

title: Dependency-license compliance (audit done; gate + THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES to follow)
description: **Audit done 17 Sep — clean:** every Composer (147), npm (158) and Cargo (524) dependency offers an AGPLv3-compatible license; nothing to remove. Full report in `LicenseAudit.md`. Remaining: (a) a CI/pre-release **gate** so a future dependency with an incompatible license (GPL-2.0-only with no permissive option, SSPL, proprietary) is caught automatically — `composer licenses` + a Cargo `cargo-deny`/`cargo-license` check + an npm scan; (b) **generate `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt`** for the bundled-server release (S-151). ffmpeg is not a linked dep (shelled out); its bundling licence is handled in S-151. Legal *review* of the policy docs is a separate human-attorney task (website W-14).

title: Cast receiver (be cast TO)
description: Make SoundChex a target other devices can **cast to** — the receive side, counterpart to the client apps' sender work (IOS-22, A-11). Two realistic paths: a **Google Cast Custom Web Receiver** (an HTML/JS receiver app registered in the Google Cast Developer Console with an app id, hosted by the server; a casting phone hands it a media URL + our token and it plays) and a **DLNA renderer** (an MediaRenderer/AVTransport service so "cast to" flows that use DLNA can target SoundChex — pairs with the DLNA output in S-153). **AirPlay receiver is not available to apps** — Apple restricts it to licensed hardware (MFi) and OS-level receivers (Apple TV/macOS), so it's out of scope. Roadmap: website (Planned). Must-have per owner.
public_summary: Cast to SoundChex — a Google Cast receiver and DLNA renderer, so a phone can send media to a SoundChex screen.

title: DLNA / UPnP media-server output
description: Advertise the library on the LAN as a DLNA/UPnP media server so devices with no SoundChex app — older smart TVs, game consoles (PS5/Xbox), network receivers, generic players — can browse and play it natively. One server-side feature for wide device reach; a lowest-common-denominator experience (no profiles/auth, basic browse, transcoding via the existing pipeline). Complements native apps, doesn't replace them. Needs SSDP discovery + a ContentDirectory service mapping the catalogue; decide whether it runs in the PHP app or a small sidecar. Roadmap: website (Planned). Cast/car integrations themselves live in the client repos (iOS IOS-21/22, Android A-10/11 — CarPlay/Android Auto + Chromecast/AirPlay sender).
public_summary: DLNA output — old TVs, consoles and receivers can play your library with no app.

title: Platform repos + product roadmap
description: One repo per toolchain that can't build together, all AGPLv3, created 17 Sep 2026: **`SoundChex`** (this repo — server + Tauri desktop macOS/Win/Linux), **`SoundChexiOS`** (Swift — iOS/iPadOS/**tvOS**), **`SoundChexAndroid`** (Kotlin/Compose — phone/tablet/**Android TV/Google TV/Fire TV**), **`SoundChexTV`** (web — **LG webOS/Samsung Tizen/Vizio SmartCast**), **`SoundChexRoku`** (BrightScript/SceneGraph), **`SoundChexWebsite`** (marketing/docs/legal). Grouped by toolchain so nothing that conflicts shares a repo and nothing that shares a runtime is duplicated (tvOS with iOS; the three Android TVs with Android). Map: `REPOS.md` (this repo). Each new repo is a scaffold (README + LICENSE + Status/Issues/Roadmap), no app code yet. The public product roadmap lives on the landing site (website W-21).

title: Bundled production server (plug-and-play self-hosting)
description: Replace `php artisan serve` (dev server, single-threaded, 2 MB upload cap, depends on Herd's `php84` by absolute path) with a bundled **PHP-FPM + Caddy** stack shipped inside the desktop app **and** as a standalone headless installer — so installing the product installs a working server with no Herd/system PHP. Plan: `BundledServer.md`; tickable steps: `BundledServerTasks.md`. **Licence decided: AGPLv3** (owner obtaining formal confirmation) — app is open-source AGPL, the paid product is the **relay-only** network (SCNet), so H.264 patent exposure is negligible (our servers never encode) and AGPL §13 stops a competitor hosting a secretly-improved fork. **AGPL is GPL-compatible, so bundle full GPL ffmpeg** (hardware + libx264 fallback, unchanged transcoder code) — no LGPL/OpenH264 detour. PHP/Caddy/SQLite all redistributable; obligations are a `LICENSE` (AGPLv3) + `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt`. **Real risk isn't packaging — it's the single-threaded assumptions** (S-123/S-87/S-93 and the network-probe/connection-watcher code were fixed *around* `artisan serve`; php-fpm is concurrent and must be re-tested). Step L (apply the AGPLv3 licence) can land now, independent of the server work. No code started; plan + tasks written.
public_summary: One-click bundled server (PHP-FPM + Caddy) — install the app and the server just works, no dependencies.

title: Smart-home / voice integrations (potential feature)
description: Let SoundChex be controlled by and surfaced in the home ecosystems: **Amazon Alexa** (a custom skill — "play … on SoundChex", queue/transport by voice, and an audio-player interface), **Samsung SmartThings**, **Apple Home / HomeKit** and **Google Home/Assistant**, plus likely **Sonos** and generic Matter/**AirPlay**/**Chromecast** targets. Each is its own surface: some are voice-command skills that call our API (needs an OAuth2 flow for account linking, not just bearer tokens, and a stable public HTTPS endpoint — ties into the SCNet relay tier), others are cast/stream targets that need the audio pipeline to hand off to a device. Big; scope one ecosystem first (Alexa skill is the most self-contained proof) and decide whether control-only or full cast. No design yet — captured so it isn't re-argued from scratch each time it comes up.
public_summary: Alexa, Google Home, Apple Home/HomeKit, SmartThings.

title: Cargo's stale absolute paths keep breaking builds, one target at a time
description: The repo move (S-112) baked `/Users/tripsittr/Documents/GitHub/SoundChex` into **every** cargo target directory, and each one only surfaces when that target is next built: `aarch64-apple-ios` broke the iOS build, `debug` broke `cargo check`, and `release` broke `build:server` — about 6.5 GB cleared across three separate discoveries, each presenting as `failed to read plugin permissions: ... app_hide.toml: No such file`, which names a Tauri permissions file and not a stale cache. Anyone hitting this reads it as a plugin problem. Worth a note in `docs/BuildingOnEachPlatform.md` and, better, a check in the build script: if any path under `src-tauri/target` names a directory that no longer exists, say so and suggest deleting that target rather than failing with someone else's error message

title: No file size is stored, so storage figures are sampled
description: `media_items` has no `size_bytes` column and `MediaItem::playbackSize()` stats the disk every time it is asked — ~12ms per 48 tracks, and the download endpoint's own comment calls it the slowest thing it does. The statistics page (S-118) therefore samples 120 files and multiplies by the track count, and says so on screen. Recording size at scan time would make it exact, remove the per-row `stat()` from the download path, and let "storage by artist" be a real total rather than an estimate

title: Nothing records where a play came from
description: "Top playlists" is computed from the plays of the tracks *on* a playlist, because no column says a play originated there — so an album track that happens to be on a playlist credits it. A `source` column on `media_plays` (album/playlist/shuffle/search) would make it exact and answers "how do I actually use this", which was on the extras list and is the one item not built

title: A "Downloaded" filter, and dimming offline
description: Done for `/app/music`; the other music surfaces are still to do (S-116). Client-side by necessity rather than choice: what a device holds lives in IndexedDB and the server has never been told, so `?downloaded=1` would be a filter that silently did nothing. That is also what makes it the one filter that keeps working with nothing reachable. Offline, an undownloaded row is **dimmed rather than hidden** — the metadata is worth reading when the audio is not there, and hiding it would make the library look like it had shrunk to whatever happened to be downloaded. The download button on a dimmed row keeps full contrast, because it is the way out of that state. Dimming keys off the connection watcher's own verdict, which now publishes `window.soundchexOffline` — the events said when it *changed* and nothing could ask what it *was*, and `navigator.onLine` knows about the interface rather than whether anything is reachable through it. 8 tests in `downloaded-filter.spec.js`, both halves checked for teeth

title: Extend the Downloaded filter to the other music surfaces
description: `/app/music` has it (S-115). Albums, artists, genres and playlists do not — and each groups rows rather than listing them, so "downloaded" means something slightly different on each: an album with three of twelve tracks on the device is neither downloaded nor not. Worth deciding that before building it, rather than picking a rule per page

title: Rebuild downloads and offline
description: Plan written: `OfflineRebuild.md`, ~9.5 days plus ~4.5 for Android. Supersedes S-06 and absorbs S-07. The system is ~3,900 lines across twelve files, passes 290 browser tests, and does not work on the phone — which is the finding rather than a bug list. **The offline specs never run on WebKit.** The `mobile` project *is* real WebKit, but its `testMatch` names twelve files and every offline spec is missing: `offline`, `offline-shell`, `offline-probe`, `library-mirror`, `write-queue` and `service-worker` are Chromium-only, where IndexedDB has a large quota, never evicts, accepts a `Blob` and does not close connections on suspend. The download *queue* is covered on WebKit; the *storage underneath it* is not. IndexedDB caps at ~1 GB — roughly one film — against **34.95 GB** of music alone, and `localUrl()` buffers a whole file into an object URL, which cannot serve range requests, so seeking in a download does not work either. Three IndexedDB databases each carry their own connection recovery, which is why S-53 sat open for a fortnight. **Scoped 9 Sep:** downloads are per-item and user-driven across all four media types (so the storage layer must stream to disk and resume a partial file — a film is gigabyte-scale); "download all" is gated on real free space, warning when it would leave the device empty and refusing when it will not fit; and all six platforms are in scope — Android, Linux, Windows 10/11, macOS, iPadOS, iOS — with Android needing its Tauri project generated from nothing. Step 0 is a `testMatch` change expecting the suite to go red; nothing else is verifiable until it does — **Broken into a tickable checklist 12 Sep: `OfflineRebuildTasks.md`** — each of Steps 0–6 plus Android as independently-verifiable sub-tasks with dependencies, a Verify line per step, and one-PR-per-step so the app keeps working until Step 6. Ready to execute incrementally; no code started.

title: Five N+1s behind the list and detail pages
description: Found by grouping a page's queries by shape. `CurrentProfile` was never registered as a singleton, so each of its 20 call sites built its own instance with an empty cache — 126 identical profile lookups on `/app/music`, 28 on `/app`. `resumePosition()` queried per track because `playerPayload()` calls it for every row in a queue (121). `track-menu.blade.php` fetched the same playlist list once per row (48). The album, artist and artists pages each ran `MediaItem::find()` inside their loop for the cover (60 and 100). Measured against the live catalogue: **`/app/music` 344 → 57 queries, `/app/albums` 68 → 4, `/app/artists` 108 → 4, `/app/genres` 205 → 46, `/app/album` 50 → 6, `/app/item` 63 → 15**. The singleton needed a cache key as well: Sanctum's test double reports the same token id for every profile, so keying on it let a capped profile read the owner's cached answer — caught by `test_two_profiles_do_not_share_a_cache_entry`, which is why the key is the token object

title: The songs list serialises its whole queue into every row
description: Measured on `/app/music` against the live catalogue: **3,026 KB of HTML for 48 songs**, of which **2,507 KB (83%) is one 26 KB queue blob repeated 96 times** — `song-row` writes `data-play="{{ $payload->toJson() }}"` on both the artwork button and the row button, so a 48-track page emits the full queue 96 times. O(n²) in the size of the list. The server is not at fault: the render is 161ms with 37ms of SQL. Emitting the queue once per list and referencing it by index takes the page to **~545 KB, 82% smaller**. Same shape on `album.blade.php` (biggest album is 49 tracks) and `playlist.blade.php`. `data-play` stays for the genuinely single-track callers — `poster.blade.php`, and `offline-shell.js`/`render.js`, which set it from JS

title: Eleven desktop playback specs waited on a media clock that never advanced
description: GitHub #25. **Unexplained, and now passing.** Frozen at `0.02322` — exactly one 1024-sample buffer at 44.1 kHz, identical to the digit across every run. Four hypotheses eliminated by testing rather than argument: the headless shell (`channel: 'chromium'`), a missing audio sink (`--mute-audio`), headed mode, and the player swapping to a downloaded blob (probed: `isBlob: false`, `localSourceUrl: null`, that path is never taken). A bare `Audio` element played fine at the same moment the app's did not, which pointed at the player — then the app's player reached `3.480802` and `player-session.spec.js` went 4/4, with the full suite 182/184 in 7 minutes against 173/184 in 42.9. Load was **higher** for the green run (6.40 against 4.9), so contention does not explain it either. Nobody knows what changed. Left open deliberately: a playback bug that fixed itself will come back, and `startPlaying()` now attaches the element's full state on failure so the next occurrence carries its own evidence instead of costing a run per guess

title: Transfer state should not live inside the catalogue it replaces
description: The carry-across in S-89 fixes the case in hand and leaves the shape of the problem: a transfer's bookkeeping is stored in the database it is overwriting, so every operation on it has to work around that. Keeping transfer state outside the catalogue — its own file — would remove the class rather than the instance. Related: after an import the receiver shows the *source's* transfer history, which means nothing here

title: Snapshot a file's own metadata at the moment it arrives
description: The embedded tags, the original filename and path, size and hash, recorded once as an `intake` version before anything renames or enriches. `metadata_versions` already holds 5,829 rows but every one has `reason = enrichment`, so the state a file arrived in exists nowhere. S-44 is exactly what that costs: the fix has to infer the original filename from the shape of a title, because the real one was overwritten and never kept

title: Transferring profiles separately from the catalogue
description: The receiver imports the whole database, which carries profiles with it — so choosing "profiles" without "the catalogue" currently does nothing. Either the option goes, or it means importing profile rows into an existing catalogue, which is a merge and a different problem

title: `npm run build:server` fails at the DMG step
description: `bundle_dmg.sh` errors, and each failure leaves a mounted disk image and `rw.*` artifacts behind that break the next attempt — so it fails worse each time until they are detached by hand. Worked around with `--bundles app`, which is enough for a local install and not for distributing one. Tauri also exits **0** on this failure, so it reads as success unless the output is read

title: No back arrow — getting out of a page means navigating all the way round
description: An artist, album or item page is reached from a list and has no way back to it except the tab bar, which lands on the top of a different screen. Needs to know where it came from rather than guessing: `history.back()` is wrong on a page opened directly or arrived at from the offline shell

title: App distribution: sideloading, stores, and what each costs
description: Reference rather than a plan, written 13 Aug with prices from that date. Overlaps `docs/BuildingOnEachPlatform.md` for the build half; what it still carries is the distribution question — sideloading against a store, and what each target charges. Kept for that

title: Reader is slow to open and to turn pages
description: Not diagnosed. Page content, OCR text and images all stream per page; the mirror does not cover the reader at all —  — **Update 17 Sep:** the web-mirror framing is superseded — the native iOS app (`SoundChexiOS`) renders detail natively, and the **book reader** is tracked there as IOS-08 (needs API reader routes). This row is about the *web/desktop* reader; keep for that surface, but the mobile answer lives in the iOS repo.

title: Artist, album and item pages are not in the device mirror
description: Six list screens are; these three are pure server round-trips, ~900ms each over the relay —  — **Update 17 Sep:** superseded for mobile — the native iOS app builds artist/album/item detail from the catalogue mirror + API (AlbumDetailView/ArtistDetailView/ShowDetailView), so the ~900ms relay round-trip this describes no longer applies on the native client. Still describes the *web/desktop* mirror; a client-detail endpoint (IOS-13) is optional there.

title: Four specs fail only in a full run
description: `downloads-batch`, `player-session`, `now-playing-sheet`, and `phone` — each verified 9 Sep to pass alone and fail in a 290-test run. **Three were removed from this list on 9 Sep**: `download-logging`, `phone-dl` and `library-refresh` fail alone and on a clean tree too, so they never belonged here — see S-110. Being filed as flakes is what stopped anyone looking at them. — `phone` added 9 Sep: `album tracks list in order` failed at test 144 of a 290-test run and passes alone, as a whole spec (7/7), and on both projects, with the same tree. Same signature as the rest — each passes alone and as a whole spec, and fails in the 282-test run. `now-playing-sheet` added 22 Aug: it failed once in a full desktop run and once alone, then passed three times alone with the same tree, so a single run of it proves nothing either way. That is the cost restated — a clean-tree comparison of one run against one run points at whichever change happens to be in the working tree. Shared IndexedDB and one seeded database across a single worker is the likely cause, but it is unproven. Until it is understood, a full-suite failure cannot be told from a real one, which is the actual cost

title: HLS adaptive streaming
description: Largest remaining item. No plan written

title: Direct route in from outside the house
description: Plan written: `DirectRemoteAccess.md`. Needs router and DNS work that is not code
public_summary: A managed relay so remote access is one toggle; an encrypted pipe to your own server.

title: Move a whole server to another machine — database, files and profiles
description: Plan written: `ServerTransfer.md`, ~7.5 days. 8,315 files, 46.3 GB, so resumability is the feature rather than polish. The receiver asks and the request sits **pending until a person on the source approves it** — no credential is copied between machines, and approval is revocable while the transfer runs. Every file hashed before and after; a mismatch is deleted rather than kept. Measured before designing: media gzips 0.4% and the database 85%

title: Buildable on Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android
description: In progress. The web app is platform-neutral; the host-specific parts are not. Address detection was macOS-only and is now per-platform. Service management is launchd and has no Windows or Linux equivalent. Android has no Tauri project generated at all. Each platform needs its toolchain documented and one real build to prove it

title: Windows and Linux client builds are untested
description: The config approach carries over unchanged, but neither has been built

title: Tailnet key expires 2027-02-09
description: The Mac drops off the tailnet that day. Disable key expiry in the Tailscale admin console

title: The browser suite takes 13 minutes on one worker
description: `workers: 1` and `fullyParallel: false`, because every test shares one SQLite database and one seeded library — parallel workers would collide. That constraint is also what causes S-04. Fixing it properly means a database per worker, which would take both from 13 minutes to a few and make a full-suite failure mean something again. Until then, run Playwright only when a change can reach a browser (AGENTS.md rule 6)

title: Device and session tracking
description: "What devices are online, using the server, and what they are doing." `device_reports` is a starting point

title: APNs push notifications
description: Paid account makes it possible; `notifications.js` already sends what push would carry

title: `MusicCredits::fromMusicBrainz()` is never called in production
description: Written and tested, but only tests call it. Enrichment always parses the credit string, so credits never get MusicBrainz's stable artist ids even when a recording matched. The better source is built and unused

title: 11 metadata sources registered but commented out
description: Discogs, Last.fm, Genius, Deezer, OMDb, Trakt, TVMaze, TVDB, Google Books, LibraryThing, Fanart.tv. Nothing breaks by their absence

title: Bundle Tailscale into the app
description: On iOS a real tunnel needs a Network Extension entitlement and its own process; the userspace version would not carry WebView traffic, which is all the traffic. Three to four weeks to match what installing Tailscale does in ten minutes. Worth revisiting if the app is ever distributed to other people

title: Build a Tailscale equivalent
description: NAT traversal and a relay network are the expensive parts, and a routable public IP means they can be skipped entirely. 6–12 months to own something that already works

title: A second updater endpoint for redundancy
description: The tailnet IP serves 301 to HTTPS and the certificate covers the MagicDNS name, so the hop fails TLS. A fallback needs a certificate, not an array entry

title: Splitting `music_metadata.artist` itself
description: It is what the file says, and `LibraryOrganizer` builds `Artist/Album/` from it. Changing it moves files on disk

title: AcoustID, Spotify and OpenSubtitles have no API key
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** All three are now key-configurable from the **Integrations** page: AcoustID and Spotify were added with the metadata-page consolidation (S-148); OpenSubtitles is added here (it already read `opensubtitles_api_key` from `SettingsService`, it just had no field). Skipped sources are logged (`MetadataPipeline` warns which skipped and why), so a missing key is visible rather than silent.

title: Three songs match no metadata provider
description: 17 Sep — **DONE (not a defect).** Verified in the live DB: items 1445 (Straw Chairs), 2002 (19 Somethin'), 2473 (Dearly Departed) still carry `match_confidence = none`. They are complete files with no provider match and will not gain metadata without a manual match — a factual state, not a fixable bug. Closed as such.

title: Three orphaned rows point at files that were re-filed
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** Verified against the live DB: the three orphaned rows (622, 623, 1107) are gone; the correctly-filed copies (3484, 3499, 2984) remain. Cleaned up during the dedup/path work (S-95/S-137).

title: Native downloads: IndexedDB caps the library at ~1 GB
description: 17 Sep — **SUPERSEDED.** Formally superseded by S-107 (offline rebuild) and, in practice, resolved by the native rebuild: the iOS app (`SoundChexiOS`) writes downloads to real disk past the IndexedDB cap. Android (`SoundChexAndroid`) will do the same (A-05).

title: Background downloads and audio stop when the app is backgrounded
description: 17 Sep — **SUPERSEDED.** Absorbed by S-107 and resolved natively: the iOS app has background audio and background `URLSession` downloads. Android to follow (A-04/A-05).

title: Listening time was never recorded
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** Added nullable `listened_seconds` + `(profile_id, created_at)` index; `saveProgress()` accumulates the forward delta with a seek guard (>90s = scrubber drag, not playback); `recordPlay()` now stamps the profile, not just the account. 7 tests in `ListeningTimeTest.php` (present on main).

title: "Download all" left every song row on the idle arrow
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** Rows marked `downloading` up front, `stored`/`failed` as each finishes; fixed the repaint-ordering and by-reference batch-button bugs. Persistence verified across SPA nav, reload, new page. 4 tests in `phone-dl.spec.js`.

title: Repo move broke services, iOS build, and artwork
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** Plists repointed off the old `Documents/GitHub/SoundChex` path; stale `src-tauri/target` + DerivedData cleared; `storage:link` re-run so the 8,293 artwork files resolve. Recurs on any move — a placeholder/startup check is follow-up (tracked in the stale-path memory), not this issue.

title: The space gate asked the browser quota and failed open
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** `checkSpace()` now fails closed on an unknown quota; shared `confirmSpace()` logs every outcome; added a `tight` warn state. Quota-scale reserve (64 MB); device-scale check belongs to native storage (S-107).

title: Shell redirect test was failing and toothless
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** `embedded-shell.spec.js` now stubs the redirect destination and tightened the wait to 2s so a broken redirect actually fails (was masked by a 5s setInterval under a 15s wait).

title: `bootstrap.sh` left SQLite `-wal`/`-shm` behind
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** `bootstrap.sh` now removes `$DB-wal` and `$DB-shm` alongside the database, so a suite killed mid-transaction no longer dies the next run with a silent disk-I/O error.

title: Music duplicates and unmatched metadata
description: 12 Sep — **DONE.** Hash-duplicate deletion done (646 merged, all sharing a file path — nothing redundant to remove; ContentGate hides them). Metadata premise proved **stale**: 100% of rows have an artist, 94% an album, 5 titles resemble a filename — getID3 tags already populated clean metadata. `match_confidence=none` means no external re-confirm, not filename titles. No safe automated title fix exists without net harm; external re-enrichment held pending owner. `music:reenrich` added (pipeline-only).

title: `useLocalSource()` in `download-button.js` was dead code
description: 17 Sep — **DONE.** Removed the unused exported function; the player/reader/watch use `localUrl()` directly and it stays. Build clean, SW re-stamped.

title: Full Spotify-style playlists across all clients
description: 17 Sep — **DONE (API PR #75, web/desktop PR #76).** API gained `PATCH /playlists/{id}` (name/description), `PUT /playlists/{id}/order` (drag reorder), `POST /playlists/{id}/cover` (image ≤5 MB); `index`/`show` return `artwork_url`, `show` adds `count` + `duration_ms` (summed after the gate). `collections.artwork_path` migration run here. Web/desktop `media/playlists` is now a cover-card grid (mosaic fallback, built in one grouped pass — no N+1) and the detail page has a big-cover header + Alpine edit modal (rename/description/cover with live preview, delete). Reorder ignores stray ids; every route is `owned()` (404, not 403). iOS shipped the matching pill + editing in 0.4.0 "Interlude" (SoundChexiOS PR #16). Tests: `PlaylistApiTest` (6) + `AlbumAndPlaylistTest` (+3).

title: Server config from the UI, not just `.env`
description: 17 Sep — **DONE (PR #73).** Admin → System → **Server Settings** edits `APP_URL`/`APP_ENV`, writes `.env` and runs `config:clear` (breaks the chicken-and-egg — the panel is reachable on localhost whatever `APP_URL` says). `EnvironmentFile` service updates individual keys. `server:detect-address` sets `APP_URL` to the best detected LAN/tailnet address (only when unset/default unless `--force`); scheduled hourly + on desktop launch, so the downloaded app is zero-config and a machine that changes networks self-heals. `docs/ServerConfiguration.md` covers panel + `.env`. **Not yet done:** this machine's `APP_URL` is still the stale `macbookair` — run `server:detect-address --force` to fix.

title: Native iOS app + client API
description: 17 Sep — **In progress, tracked in `SoundChexiOS/`.** The client API is built and merging (PR #71). The native app (browse/playback/downloads/playlists/admin/detail/lyrics) is on `github.com/tripsittr/SoundChexiOS`, PRs #1–#8. See that repo's `Plans/Issues.md`. Desktop stays Tauri.

title: Metadata Sources admin page removed
description: 17 Sep — **DONE (PR #72).** The provider keys are configured on the Integrations page now (`metadataRows()` renders/saves them), so the standalone page was redundant. Removed it and updated the stale Integrations doc comments. (The earlier S-145 — the Tauri offline-UI "Phase 3" — is superseded by the native iOS app, S-146, and its abandoned branches were deleted.)

title: Offline native downloads + playback
description: 15 Sep — **DONE, merged (PR #69), device-verified.** Downloads write to real disk (native backend, past the iOS ~1GB IndexedDB cap), stream large files, self-describing on-disk manifests; offline detection and offline playback both work on the phone. Root cause was Tauri v2 denying app commands on the remote server origin (bridge not injected + no ACL permission) — fixed via initialization_script_for_all_frames + build.rs AppManifest::commands. The offline **UI** match (artwork cache, full renderers) continues as S-145 (Phase 3).

title: Service install wrote to /Library/LaunchAgents and failed
description: 15 Sep — Fixed. `HostServices::agentPath()` built `(\$_SERVER['HOME'] ?? getenv('HOME')) . '/Library/LaunchAgents/…'`; from a context with no HOME (launchd, the desktop shell's service command, cron) the prefix is empty and the path collapsed to the root `/Library/LaunchAgents`, which no non-root process may write. `??` did not help — `\$_SERVER['HOME']` can be `''`, which it passes through. `log()` had the same bug against `/Library/Logs`. Fixed with one `homeDir()` resolving HOME from `\$_SERVER`, env, then the passwd entry, returning null rather than a root path; callers refuse with a clear message. Server-side, live on deploy. `HostServicesTest` +2, teeth-checked against the old code. PHP 572

title: Songs repeated across pages, others missing
description: 14 Sep — Fixed. Found on the phone, never phone-specific. `MediaBrowser::grid()` ordered by `created_at` alone — not a total order, since **1,124 tracks share one `created_at`** (a whole import in one second), so the paginator returned tied rows in engine-arbitrary order that differed between the page-1 and page-2 queries: a song on both, another on neither. Fixed with a unique `media_items.id` tiebreaker; album/artist pages got tiebreakers on their group keys too (case-tie, milder). Server-side, live on reload. Verified on the real library: 0 overlap between pages 1 and 2. `BrowsePaginationTest` (2) — with a recorded caveat that in-memory SQLite can mask order instability, so the id-in-ORDER-BY assertion is the real guard

title: Two admin tiers: library vs server, with a panel floor
description: 12 Sep — Done. The panel had no floor — `canAccessPanel()` returned true for everyone and each screen refused individually, and most screens asked for per-page permissions (`Access:MetadataSettings`, `ViewAny:Music`) that were never created, so they were **owner-only by accident**. Added `Access:LibraryAdministration` (migration creates the permission only — granting is per profile, since `Profile::can()` reads profile_permissions and ignores roles; owner short-circuits) and `Profile::canAdministerLibrary()`, which server administration implies. `RestrictsToAdmins::canAccess()` now passes on the library-admin floor **or** a screen's own narrow grant, so a library admin reaches every content screen while a member granted just `ViewAny:Music` still reaches only that — the existing fine-grained path is preserved (per owner's call; the two readings genuinely conflicted and this was the chosen one). `canAccessPanel()` blocks a profile with **zero** admin-side permissions at the door rather than admitting it to be bounced page by page. Metadata Sources is now reachable by library admins (was owner-only); Integrations/*arr stay server-admin. Permissions UI already existed on ProfileResource — improved it to show 'Library administration' / 'Server administration' with descriptions and lead ordering rather than raw permission names. 9 tests in `LibraryAdministrationAccessTest`; 2 existing tests (`AccessControlTest`, `ServerAdministrationAccessTest`) reconciled with the new floor. Migration run on this machine after a `.backup`. **Not merged**: whether to fold Metadata Sources into the Integrations page is left open — the two coexist cleanly

title: 1,303 items pointed at the old repo path; 11 of 14 books unreadable
description: 12 Sep — **Verified against the live library, after a `.backup`.** `media_items.file_path` was absolute for 1,306 rows, 1,303 of them under the pre-move `Documents/GitHub/SoundChex/...` prefix — and `ReaderController@show` 404s on a missing file, so those books could not be opened at all. The files were fine on disk; only the stored paths were stale. Dry-run first (working agreement: verify before writing): 1,297 rewrote cleanly, 6 resolved to files that did not exist, 0 collisions. Rewrote all 1,303 to **relative** paths like the other 7,032 rows — `absoluteFilePath()` resolves those against the disk, so this is the shape the code prefers and it immunises them against the next move (the exact failure class as S-112/S-127). The 6 missing turned out to be duplicate rows of the re-filed originals (S-45 family): cleared 7 then 3 more, all with zero plays and no progress, files untouched. After: 8,328 items, 0 absolute paths, and only 2 genuinely-lost files remain (ids 3410/3887 — a Royal Blood video and an Aphex Twin set with no twin on disk). All 11 books now open 200; music item pages 200 with the stream file present

title: `soundchex-addresses.json` was unauthenticated and CORS-open
description: 12 Sep — Fixed. The endpoint listed **every** address the server answers on — LAN IP, tailnet hostname, relay — to anyone, with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Reaching one route does not entitle a caller to a map of the others, and an outsider on the public relay had no business learning the LAN address. Now behind `auth` with the CORS header dropped. Its only caller is `failover.js`, a same-origin fetch from pages already behind auth (cookie rides along) whose `!response.ok` branch falls back to the stored list, so a signed-out fetch degrades rather than breaks. `/soundchex.json` stays public and minimal by design — it only says "this is a SoundChex server on build X", which discloses nothing. 4 tests, including one asserting the identity payload never grows past {app, version, build} without a fight

title: Windows PHP has no CA bundle, so every HTTPS request failed
description: 12 Sep — Fixed. GitHub #4. Windows PHP ships without a CA bundle, so transfers, TMDB, MusicBrainz, artwork and subtitles all failed with `cURL error 60` until someone hand-edited php.ini. Installed `composer/ca-bundle` and pointed every outbound call at it via `Http::globalOptions([verify => CaBundle::getSystemCaRootBundlePath()])` in `AppServiceProvider::boot()` — finds the system bundle where one exists (a no-op on macOS/Linux) and falls back to the shipped pem on Windows. Verified: outbound HTTPS to TMDB returns 204 through the global verify path. The transfer error message that blamed php.ini was updated — it now describes a genuinely bad certificate, clock skew or TLS interception, since a missing bundle is no longer possible

title: An Integrations page, and optional Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. One page under System answering "what is this install connected to?" — previously spread across a settings page, an env file and a container that may or may not be running, with nothing saying which. Every integration is a row: **Set up** when it has no key, **Manage** and **Unlink** when it does, both opening the same modal. Fifteen rows, one form, because the question is identical in each case. **Metadata sources are listed but still configured on their own page**, deliberately: they are read-only keys and enriching the catalogue *is* library administration, so a library admin should keep them — while this page is gated to server administration because acquisition reaches the network, spends disk and decides what arrives on the machine. Merging them would either lock metadata away from the right people or open acquisition to the wrong ones. A Docker Compose stack ships alongside (Radarr, Sonarr, Lidarr, qBittorrent), with `php artisan arr:setup` deriving every path and the host UID/GID so nothing has to be hand-edited; web UIs bind to loopback only, since these have no auth until it is set up inside each app and this machine is on a tailnet. **The apps are never bundled** — they are GPLv3 and shipping them would make us a redistributor, App Store review would refuse a bundled torrent client, and it is ~400MB most installs will not use. Detected-and-offered, the same pattern AGENTS.md already mandates for ffmpeg and tesseract. **Readarr excluded**: retired upstream in 2025 with an unreliable metadata backend. **No indexers ship or are configured** — the stack is inert until someone adds one by hand. Keys stored encrypted via `SettingsService`; the modal never pre-fills a stored key, because they are encrypted precisely so the panel cannot read them back. 12 tests

title: A household shared one place in every book
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. Two faults that hid each other, both dating from when profiles were added to a schema that predated them. `profile_id` was never added to `ReadingProgress::$fillable`, so although `updateOrCreate()` keys the row on the profile, mass assignment **silently dropped it on insert** — every row was written with a null profile whoever was reading, and the household shared one position in every book. That does not read as a bug; it reads as the app forgetting where you were. And the unique index still said `(media_item_id, user_id)` — a household shares one login, so the moment the first fault was fixed the second reader's save was **refused with a 500**. Fixed together: `profile_id` fillable, and a migration swapping the index to `(media_item_id, profile_id)` with a plain index on `(media_item_id, user_id)` for pre-profile rows, which SQLite keeps distinct because every NULL is distinct. `down()` deliberately fails once two profiles have a position in one book — reversing means destroying someone's place. **Found by tests written for something else** (S-135): they 500'd on a constraint nobody was looking for. Live database has 2 rows, both null-profile — the fingerprint — and they stay readable via the account fallback but cannot be attributed now

title: A book read offline lost its page
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. The reader's progress save caught its failures and did nothing: "losing one position update isn't worth interrupting reading" — true of one update, wrong about a whole session read offline, which is every update. The player had queued its writes for a while (the position of a film watched on a train); a book read on the same train dropped them. Reader writes now go into the same `soundchexWrites` queue, keyed per item so a long session leaves one entry rather than one per page turn, stamped with when the page was actually read rather than when the connection returned. Because a queued write arrives late, `ReaderController::saveProgress()` gained the staleness guard `MediaCenterController` already had — a position older than what the server holds is refused, so reconnecting a phone cannot rewind reading done on another device. 6 tests; each of the three fixes turns a different one red on revert. **Not yet covered**: the browser half — a real offline read then reconnect — has feature tests against the endpoint but no e2e test

title: Logging review: failures that said nothing
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. Audited every `catch` against the working agreement's "log anything that can fail". Most of the app was already right, and the raw counts misled — many silent catches are the rule's own exemption (private-browsing storage, expected offline, health probes that mean "can't tell, assume not running"), and several files using `report()` looked unlogged to a grep for `Log::`. Three real gaps fixed. **The player silently streaming a downloaded track**: if reading the local blob threw, it fell back to the network with nothing recorded — the user downloaded it and is now on mobile data with no evidence why (note `localUrl()` returns null without throwing for a merely-absent file, so a throw here means the store itself is unhappy). **Two file-move failures** in `EnrichMediaItemJob` and `TranscodeMediaJob` that called `report($e)` and so produced a stack trace with no item id — a full disk fails every item in a scan identically, and the question afterwards is always which files are still in the inbox. Now logged with item, title and path

title: Security and performance review
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. Full pass over the app, written up in `Documentation & Planning/Security/findings/2026-09-11-security-and-performance-review.md`. One real vulnerability (S-129), two performance defects (S-130), one hardening change, one informational note. The **audited-clean** half is the part worth keeping: route auth probed unauthenticated (all 302), API auth and throttling, updater path traversal probed (all 404), the transfer token leak re-probed to confirm the earlier fix holds, SQL injection across every builder call site, mass assignment on every model, and the search highlighter's escape-then-substitute-sentinels approach. Recorded with its evidence because next time "we looked at it" is worth as much as "we fixed it", and without the evidence it cannot be told apart from not having looked. Hardened `TopItemsTable`'s raw `instr()` — ids interpolated into a raw fragment, **not exploitable today** since they come from the database, but a shape that becomes an injection the moment its source changes. Left alone deliberately: `policy.blade.php` and `terms.blade.php` use `{!! !!}` but are unrouted and unincluded — the finding worth recording is that they are dead, so escaping must be revisited if either is ever wired up. Full suite 526 passed

title: A download-persistence test that failed 4 runs in 5
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. `downloads-batch.spec.js` "a queue survives the app closing" (mobile/WebKit) enqueued three downloads, reloaded, and asserted two were still stored. **The queue was never broken** — `resumeDownloads()` runs on load and immediately re-enqueues everything it finds, and the fixture URLs are a few hundred bytes, so by the time the test could ask, the queue had legitimately drained. The test was watching resume work correctly and calling it a regression. Fixed by reading `localStorage` *before* the reload, then polling for the drain — which asserts the half that actually matters, that the app picks the work back up. 6/6 from 1/5; teeth checked by making `persist()` write `[]`. **Two process notes.** Reverting S-132 made it pass, so it briefly looked caused by that — it was not: the *original* code fails 4 in 5, and **one run per side is not a bisect when the test is non-deterministic**. And the first hypothesis (a race between the reload and the 4-second runner timers) was wrong: replacing them with promises that never settle changed nothing, and a direct log showed a consistent `["803"]` rather than the varying results a race produces — that consistency is what pointed at resume

title: A finished batch download never left its spinner
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. A batch completed, the file landed in IndexedDB, and the row's icon span forever; navigating away and back cleared it. **Two guards, each correct alone.** `runBatch()` marks every row `downloading` before starting, so a long batch does not leave the list looking untouched. `paintIconDownloadStates()` skips any button already reading `downloading`, because a repaint landing mid-transfer otherwise resets a live download's spinner to idle — indistinguishable from a tap that did nothing. Together they deadlock: every row in the batch reads `downloading`, so the repaint skips exactly the rows whose outcome it was meant to write. Hard to see because **nothing was broken** — the queue emitted `started → finished → idle`, the fetch returned 200 with all 119 KB, quota was 2.1 GB against 835 KB used. Only the icon disagreed; the bug was in who was allowed to *write* the state. Fixed by marking each row from its own settled result, which the failure path already did for the same reason. Found by the Playwright suite during S-131, then checked against pre-review code and confirmed **pre-existing**, not caused by that work. Teeth: removing the one added line turns both tests red. Downloads spec 18/18

title: Header injection through `Content-Disposition`
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. Both streaming endpoints built the header by hand with `addslashes($item->title)` — which escapes quotes but leaves **CR and LF untouched**, and Symfony stores a header value verbatim, so a title containing `\r\n` terminates the header and starts one of the attacker's choosing. Reachable because titles are not ours: they come from tags in imported files and from TMDB, MusicBrainz and Open Library, and the codebase otherwise treats them as trusted. Replaced with `ResponseHeaderBag::makeDisposition()`, which refuses control characters and also fixes something the hand-rolled version got wrong — RFC 6266 `filename*` encoding, so a Cyrillic or accented title is no longer mangled. Proof on revert: `'inline; filename="Innocent\r\nX-Injected: yes"'`. 3 tests in `HeaderInjectionTest`, all red on revert. Found during the S-131 review

title: The home page built eight rails per type and used one
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. `home()` called `rowsForType($type)` — the **entire** browse page: four fixed rails plus up to four genre rails, eight queries each carrying a full eager-load batch — and kept `[0]`. Seven-eighths of the work was built and discarded, once per media type, and it **scaled**: the genre rails derive from how many distinct genres exist, so 58 queries at four items became 69 after adding forty. Separately, `base()` eager-loaded all four metadata tables for every query, so a music query asked `movie_metadata`, `show_metadata` and `book_metadata` for rows it knew were not there — three always-empty round-trips per batch. And `hero()` ran `base()` twice, discarding the second whenever artwork existed, which is the normal case. **`/app`: 140 → 23 queries**; `/app/music` 57 → 36 without being touched. 6 tests in `HomePageCostTest`. **Two of them were wrong when first written and still green** — the hero test searched the whole page, where both films render, and once scoped still passed because two rows created in the same second tie on `latest()`. Both noted in the findings document, because a test that cannot go red is worse than none

title: Server administration split from library administration
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. The admin panel does two jobs, and only one of them belongs in the app you browse with: `Services` can stop the web server that is serving the page you are reading it on, `ServerTransfer` copies tens of gigabytes between machines and deletes on failure, `Network` decides which addresses clients race, `DeviceReports` is diagnostics. All four now sit behind `Access:ServerAdministration` via a new `RestrictsToServerAdmins` trait, replacing four separate per-page permissions — the four pages are one decision ("is this person responsible for the machine?") and four permissions is four chances to grant three of them. The System group is hidden from the sidebar *and* the pages refuse with 403, because Filament resolves a page by URL whether or not anything links to it. **Gated on the profile rather than on which app is asking**: a User-Agent marker would have been forgeable and would not hold in a browser, where the same pages are reachable on the LAN today. The owner short-circuits, so a household cannot lock its own administrator out. Statistics moved into Media Library beside the resources it describes, and System is now declared last in `navigationGroups()` so the order is a decision rather than discovery order. Migration creates the permission (one row, backed up first) — without it the pages would be owner-only with no way to grant access short of a database edit. **Note**: a trait constant cannot be read as `Trait::CONST` in PHP, so the name lives on `Profile::SERVER_ADMINISTRATION`. 6 tests, and the teeth check turns three red including the 403-vs-200 one that distinguishes refusing from merely hiding

title: Top items as a real Filament table, with artwork
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. The hand-rolled `<table>` was the reason the page looked worse than the dashboard, which uses `TableWidget` for Recently Added — artwork, badges and chrome that follows the panel instead of drifting from it. Only the *item* list became a table: an artist or a genre has no artwork of its own, so a table there would be chrome around two columns, and those stay compact lists. **One bug worth remembering**: an `ImageColumn` on `cover_image_url` rendered the placeholder for all 24 rows, because the stored value is a path relative to the storage disk and segments carry spaces, commas and apostrophes from artist and album names — only `MediaItem::coverUrl()` encodes them. Verified: 24 real images, 0 placeholders, including `Kurt Vile/b'lieve i'm goin down.../Pretty Pimpin`. Row order is forced with `instr()` over the play ranking, because `whereIn` returns id order and the table would otherwise disagree with its own heading

title: Dashboard trimmed (was S-125; renumbered — two machines assigned S-125 on the same day), and pointed at the statistics page
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. "Plays this week" removed — the statistics page answers it far better and the two were duplicating. The dashboard keeps what is operational: items, storage, needs review, recently added, network health. A **More stats** header action links through, hidden from anyone who cannot open that page. Deliberately *not* trimmed further: genre split and recently added were considered and kept, because they answer "what is in here" rather than "what was listened to"

title: "Download all" removed from the songs page
description: PR #55–57, merged 11–12 Sep — Merged. Scoped to the button only: `/app/downloadable`, `runBatch()` and the album/playlist/track-menu batch buttons all stay, because those still power "Download this album". Two library-wide tests went with it; `download-logging` self-skips (it already guarded on the button existing) and is now 2 skipped rather than deleted, so it comes back if the button ever does. Found while removing it: `runBatch()`'s completion code re-found `[data-download-library]` by name, so an *album* download wrote its outcome onto a button on a different page — and once the library button was gone, onto nothing. It now re-finds by whichever marker the button it started from carries

title: The Integrations modals' "Open Lidarr/Radarr/Sonarr" links were dead in the packaged app
description: 12 Sep — **Verified — the owner clicked Open in the packaged app and the browser opened.** Two buried causes, both producing identical total silence, which is why three earlier JS-level fixes were each correct and each changed nothing. **First: the binary was stale.** All the code was right — `data-open-external` markup, the delegated listener, `tauri-plugin-opener` in Cargo.toml and `lib.rs` — but both apps in /Applications predated it: `strings` found `plugin:notification` and zero `plugin:opener`. Rebuilt and reinstalled both. **Still dead. Second, the real killer: the capability had no `windows` key.** Diagnosed by making the silence talk — a temporary probe in `external-links.js` reported into `laravel.log` from inside the release webview (which has no devtools): IPC injected fine, but `Command plugin:opener — open_url not allowed by ACL`. The `remote.urls` patterns were *not* the problem — replicated Tauri's exact matching with the same `urlpattern 0.3.0` crate; every pattern matched the panel URL. The cause is in `resolve_access` (tauri 2.11.5, `ipc/authority.rs`): a command is admitted only when a `webviews` **or** `windows` glob matches, an omitted key is an empty list, and an empty list matches *nothing* — so **every permission in the capability (opener, notification, updater) was denied in both apps, on local and remote pages alike**, silently. The template's `"windows": ["main"]` is not decoration; added `"windows": ["*"]`, rebuilt, probe flipped from ACL-denied to `invalid args` (the probe sends a wrong type on purpose, so an error *from the command itself* proves the gate passed), owner's click confirmed. Probe and its `/dev/tauri-probe` route removed after. **Bonus finding: `window.alert` is a no-op in wry on macOS** — the ACL denial reached the alert line and showed nothing, so the failure path now renders a DOM banner instead. Notification and updater calls from web pages were presumably broken this whole time too — worth re-testing them. 98 Vitest green after

title: A real application menu for the desktop apps
description: this branch — Built and compiles clean (`cargo build`, 42 MB binary); **not yet driven in the app**. The shell had no menu code at all and took Tauri's default, whose File submenu holds only Close Window — so Cmd-R did nothing, in a window onto a served web app where a stale page is an ordinary state. Refresh is `CmdOrCtrl+R`, the reflex everyone already has, and reloads **every** webview rather than the focused one: the server app opens a second window and refreshing one leaves the other on a pre-deploy page. `eval("location.reload()")` rather than re-navigating, which is what the browser's own refresh does and keeps scroll position. `Menu::default()` composes its submenus inline and returns a finished menu, so there is no File submenu to reach into — the menu is mirrored and extended instead, which means the rest of it is ours to keep in step if Tauri's default changes. **Also cleared 1.6 GB of stale `target/debug`**: the same `Documents/GitHub/SoundChex` path that broke the iOS build (S-112) was baked into the debug cache too, and `cargo check` failed with the same misleading "failed to read plugin permissions" error. **Extended 11 Sep to nine items**, all of which the server app gets too — both binaries call `soundchex_lib::run()` and differ only in config. File: Refresh, **Hard Refresh** (`CmdOrCtrl+Shift+R`, which clears the caches *and* unregisters the service worker before reloading — a plain reload still serves the JS the worker already had, which is the actual post-deploy stale-page problem), Reconnect to Server (re-runs the address race through `failover.check()`, because staying on a working-but-slow relay is the failure that hides), Copy Server Address. View: Library `Cmd-1`, Admin `Cmd-2`. Help: Open Logs Folder (`~/Library/Logs/SoundChex` — where the 4.6 MB serve log sat unread because macOS TCC forced the logs out of the repository), Open Database Folder, Restart Services. **One thing that needed care**: the server app loads a *local* `server.html`, so `location.origin` there is `tauri://localhost` — Copy Address would have handed over a meaningless address and `/app` would have resolved inside the bundle. Both now prefer that page's own `ORIGIN`. **Built and installed 11 Sep**: both `SoundChex Server.app` and `SoundChex.app` are in /Applications with all nine ids verified in each binary, and the web server stayed up throughout — the app and the launchd agents are separate things. The DMG step succeeded for both, which S-74 says is not reliable; worth noting it works from a clean `release` target. Still not *driven*: the items compile and are present, but nobody has clicked them

title: The dashboard's storage tile stat'd every file on every load
description: this branch — Verified — **57ms cold, 3ms cached**, against a version that loaded all 8,338 rows and called `filesize()` on each. Now samples 200 files at random and scales, cached for an hour: a library's size does not change between two page loads. Random rather than the first 200 because the earliest imports here are music and the latest are films, two orders of magnitude apart. Still an estimate — the real fix is the `size_bytes` column in S-119

title: `NetworkHealth` reported the server unreachable from the server
description: this branch — Verified — `network:probe` now reports **3 of 3 answering** (30ms tailnet, 139ms LAN, 262ms Funnel) where the dashboard had said "0 of 3, clients cannot reach this server". The cause was the measurement itself: `probe()` HTTP-requested the server's own addresses *during a page render*, and `artisan serve` is single-threaded, so it waited on the process that would have answered and timed out against itself. `probe()` is now read-only, `measure()` does the work from a scheduled command every five minutes, and the Network page's Retest queues `ProbeNetworkJob` rather than blocking. The widget distinguishes **not measured yet** from measured-and-failing, because saying the second when the first is true is how a dashboard trains people to ignore it. My earlier claim that the LAN address was also stale was wrong — `192.168.1.169` is correct and answers; I had mistyped it when testing. 6 tests, and the key one (`reading the probe makes no requests`) turns red if the inline probe ever returns

title: Statistics for every media type, behind a tab group
description: this branch — Verified — all four tabs query cleanly against the real library, including the **empty** one, which is the case most likely to divide by zero. `MusicStatistics` became `LibraryStatistics` with the type as injected state (`->for($type)`) rather than six hardcoded `where type = music` filters, and a `shape()` map naming each type's two groupings and metadata table: artist/album for music, director/studio for film, creator/network for a show, author/publisher for a book. Show plays roll up to the series through `COALESCE(parent_id, id)`, or twenty episodes fill the list as twenty entries. Metadata tables are **left**-joined — an inner join silently dropped every film enrichment had not reached, which reads as a smaller library rather than a gap. Today: music 8,319 items / 2,321 artists / 513.9h, films 5 / 2 directors, books 14 / 9 authors, shows 0. 16 tests

title: Music statistics page in the admin panel
description: this branch — Verified — renders 200 in **361ms with 38 queries** against the real 8,319-track library, and 13 tests in `MusicStatisticsTest.php`. Custom Blade at **Library → Statistics**, gated on `View:MusicStatisticsPage` through `RestrictsToAdmins`. One date range and one profile filter at the top drive every figure, applied in a single private `plays()` builder so no two sections can disagree about what "last 30 days" means. **Redone 11 Sep after review**: CSS bars replaced with seven real Chart.js widgets on Filament's own `ChartWidget`, which ships with the panel and was already used by `GenreSplit` — no new dependency, and no Apex plugin needed. Top artists and storage are horizontal bars (long names), genres a doughnut (proportion is the question), the clock and weekday vertical bars, discovery and library-vs-listened stacked. Laid out **two across** on `xl` rather than stacked full-width, which is what made the page endless, and the eight headline figures are an inline row rather than eight cards taking a screen to say eight numbers. The charts are Livewire components embedded in the view and keyed on the range and profile, so changing either remounts them — widgets have their own lifecycle and would otherwise not see the page's filters. Each repeats `canView()` rather than inheriting the page's gate: Livewire resolves a component by name, so a chart is reachable without the page. **Second review pass**: every chart now carries its own subtitle naming the window, whose listening it is, and *what it counts* — "Last 30 days · everyone · plays per artist, top 10" — because a bar labelled only with a number leaves the reader guessing at the unit, and plays, listening seconds and estimated bytes are three different things on one screen. Axis titles and tooltips too: the artist tooltip carries tracks and minutes alongside the play count, since twelve plays cannot be told from twelve skips otherwise, and the genre doughnut shows each slice's share. Layout weighted rather than seven equal boxes — discovery full width because a thirty-day time series does not fit in half a screen. **The in-app disclosure banners were removed**: explaining to the owner of a private server that 504 of his own plays predate a column is changelog material, not UI. The unattributed row survives in the per-profile table as data, without the apology. `getHeading()` and `getDescription()` must be `public` and return `string — Htmlable — null` to match `ChartWidget` — a narrower signature is a fatal error at render. **Three bugs the tests caught before shipping:** `diffInDays()` returns a *float* in Carbon 3, so `=== 1` never matched and every streak was reported as 1 — plausible enough to have shipped unnoticed; `size_bytes` does not exist on `media_items` at all, so storage is now a sampled estimate (108 files, ~5.0 MB average) rather than an invented total or 8,319 filesystem reads per load; and `file_path` is relative to the storage disk for most rows, so reading the column directly found zero files — it goes through `absoluteFilePath()` now. Real numbers today: 513.9h across 8,319 tracks, 405 tracks and 283 of 2,321 artists ever played, peak listening hour 1am

title: Four mobile specs failed on their own, on a clean tree, and were filed as flakes
description: this branch — Verified — **77/77 on the whole mobile project**. The headline cause was one line of config: the `mobile` project ran with Playwright's default `serviceWorkers: 'allow'`, and a worker controls this origin — so requests it answers on the page's behalf never reach `page.route()` *or* `context.route()`. `download-logging:36` aborted `/app/downloadable`, watched the listing succeed anyway, and saw `requestfinished` fire for a request its own handler had never been consulted about. That reads as a timing problem, which is why the first three attempts at it — reloading with the route installed, routing on the context, waiting for the failure rather than sleeping — were all wrong. Now `serviceWorkers: 'block'` for that project; `service-worker.spec.js` runs on desktop and keeps them. **Two real app bugs came out of the same investigation**: `drain(run)` applied one runner to the whole queue, so whichever `enqueue()` started the drain decided how every later item was fetched and a queued download could silently never run (the runner now travels with its entry); and the click handler wrote `stored` onto the button captured at click time, which a library refresh had replaced via `main.replaceChildren()` — file on the device, icon saying otherwise. `paintIconDownloadStates()` also no longer resets a button mid-transfer, and announces itself so a test can wait for it rather than sleep. Two test-only fixes: the launch sync is a *full* one on a fresh database and legitimately redraws, and `record('test:reset')` only *appends* — it never cleared the `sessionStorage` buffer it was meant to reset

title: The cancel e2e spec drove a state where Cancel is deliberately not offered
description: `a589f20` — Verified — 4/4 in the browser here, and checked for teeth by breaking the Cancel button. The spec pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:9` and expected a cancellable transfer. That address is refused, so the transfer ended `failed`, and `server-transfer.blade.php` offers Cancel only for `requested`, `approved`, `running` and `paused` — a finished transfer has nothing left to stop on the other machine. The click waited 30s for a button that would never render. The app was right and the spec was wrong. Asking cannot be pointed at this server either: `artisan serve` is single threaded, so its own request waits on the process serving the page that made it and times out at 20s. Now asks `tests/e2e/stub-source-server.js` on 8198, which answers any POST with a request id, leaving the transfer `requested` and cancellable. Second fault, also fixed: rows were matched page-wide, so the closing `toHaveCount(0)` counted leftovers from earlier runs and could never reach zero — rows are now keyed by `wire:key` and every assertion is scoped to the one row. The key is a real fix as well as a test seam: a keyless `@foreach` lets Livewire reuse the wrong DOM node across near-identical rows. Checked for teeth by breaking the Cancel button, which turns it red. Written on `a5`, where there is no `.env.e2e`, so it could not be run before it landed

title: Working agreement between the two agents
description: `a589f20` — Verified — PR #32 reviewed and approved by A5, who independently checked every factual claim rather than taking it from the text, and caught two things: that an `a5` approval cannot attest to browser behaviour (no Playwright there), and that `AGENTS.md` documented Laravel 12 / Livewire 3 against a `composer.lock` holding v13.15.0 / v4.3.1. Both fixed before merge. 451 PHP · 87 Vitest green on `main` after. GitHub #31, set by the owner and in force now. **Mac writes every fix; `a5` writes none.** `a5` reports logs, findings, errors, reproductions and measurements on the issue — that is the input fixes are built from. **Order:** `a5` claims the issue → Mac fixes, commits, pushes, opens a PR → **`a5` tests and reviews it fully and approves** → Mac merges → both run real tests → Mac closes the issue and tells the owner. Mac does not merge before `a5`'s approval. **"Real tests" explicitly excludes PHPUnit, Pest, Vitest and Playwright** — those still have to pass but do not close anything. Real means driving the application: requests through the app, a transfer actually run between machines, a file actually played, a page actually loaded on a device. Justified by the Cancel button, which shipped with nine passing tests behind it and did nothing when clicked. **Sign-offs**: `— Mac` from `macbookair`, `— A5` from the Windows machine, on every comment and issue, because "it passes here" means different things on a machine with Playwright and the full library than on one with neither. **What an `a5` approval covers**: `a5` has no Playwright, so its approval never means "works in a browser" — it names what it covered (PHP, Vitest, real requests against the running app, reading the diff) and any browser-shaped risk it could not test, which Mac then tests here before merging. Conversely `a5` is the *receiving* machine in a transfer, so transfer behaviour cannot be verified from the Mac side alone — six of seven transfer bugs on 23 Aug were only visible there. Written up in `docs/WorkingWithTwoAgents.md`

description: this commit — Found because S-100 worked: the transfer stopped on a 401 and said so, then the watcher restarted it because the source said the request was still `approved`. `publicState()` returned `expired` only for a *pending* request past its time; an approved one kept saying `approved` for ever. `isUsable()` had always refused it, so the 401s were right — the published status was the part that lied, and the receiver believed it and retried a token that could never work. Both states report `expired` now; denied and revoked keep their own names, because a decision someone made is more use than the clock running out. description: this commit — Two were fixed by S-98. Of the rest, `LibraryOrganizer::toRelative()` stored `media\library\…` because `realpath()` returns backslashes there, which is the other end of the S-98 mismatch that gave one film nine rows. `ConversionFiler`'s guard against flattening an organised library compared paths with `DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR` against a `Storage::path()` that mixes both — so **the guard did nothing on Windows and the filer moved real files it should have refused**. `HostServicesTest` errored on a macOS-only folder and left its log behind; it creates and removes what it needs now. **446 tests, 445 passing, 1 skipped, nothing failing** — the first green run on this machine, which matters because four tests written today could not have failed and "still the same six" is indistinguishable from "and one new one"

description: this commit — Found on transfer 9, which reported `running` for half an hour having copied nothing while the worker was healthy: `The server answered 401.` Tokens last four hours from approval, and when one expires every remaining file answers 401 — but the receiver treated each as *that file* failing, so a dead token was retried through **6,964 items that could never arrive**. 401 and 403 now end the transfer with an error saying to ask again and approve it on the other machine; what has already copied is kept so a fresh approval resumes. An ordinary 404 still fails only that file, which is tested as hard. This is what stopped the real transfer at 14 of 6,995

title: Every scan catalogued the whole library again on Windows
description: this commit — GitHub #16/#18, and most of what "tons of dupes all over the library" actually was. One film held **nine rows for one path**. The scanner keys its known list on `Storage::path()` — `C:\…\storage\app/private\media\…`, mixed separators — and looks it up with `getRealPath()`'s `C:\…\media\…`. Never equal as strings, so every file looked new on every scan and the count grew for ever. Both sides go through one canonical spelling now; case is folded only where the filesystem ignores it, since on Linux `Song.mp3` and `song.mp3` are two files. **Fixed two of the six S-86 failures as a side effect** — those tests were describing this bug

Both machines were on a **relayed** tailnet (`relay "lax"`) rather than a direct connection, which is slower to establish. The connect timeout is 30s now; the request timeouts are untouched, because a server that accepts and then goes quiet is a different problem and should still be given up on

title: The manifest sent absolute paths, so files landed in a mirror of the source's filesystem
description: this commit — Caught 31 files into transfer 9, before 47 GB of it. `SourceController::manifest()` sent `file_path` claiming it was relative; on the source it is absolute, so the receiver joined `/Users/tripsittr/…` onto its own storage root. The manifest now derives the path from the storage root, and the receiver refuses anything that will not land under its media root — it wrote wherever it was told, which handed a remote machine the choice of where to write on this one. Worst part was quieter: the imported catalogue carries the source's paths too, and `absoluteFilePath()` returns null for them here, so **every item in the imported library resolved to nothing** — the import now rewrites them, and `library:relative-paths` repairs one imported before that existed. 11 tests; removing the guard turns 9 red

title: A transfer destroyed its own record half way through
description: this commit — The catalogue import replaces the whole database, and `transfers`/`transfer_items` live in it — so the arriving catalogue overwrote the running transfer and its 8,309-row work list with the source's own bookkeeping, and `RunTransferJob` fatalled on `wants()` on null. Seen on transfer 9: the catalogue imported correctly and the file copy could never begin. The rows are snapshotted before the swap and written back after, and the job stops rather than fatalling if they are still missing. The first test written for this could not fail — on `:memory:` the row is never at risk — so it asserts the carry-across through its log line instead

Five processes hold the catalogue, and the one renaming is the queue worker itself, so it could not succeed even with everything else stopped. The connection is now dropped first and `rename()` tried, then the contents written over the existing file when that still fails. Two further faults fixed with it: the backup omitted 4.3 MB of `-wal`, and a catalogue that could not be placed was deleted rather than kept for the retry. 3 tests; removing the fallback or the sidecar cleanup turns one red each

title: Films and shows were not being classified correctly
description: this commit — **50 of 159 films in the real library were television** — measured, not estimated. Two causes. `EpisodeParser::parse()` answered two different questions with one value: "is this television?" decided the type, and "can this be filed?" decided whether a real file moves. Every case it refused for filing was catalogued as a **film**, which is all 48 Simpsons season-zero specials. Separately the `S06X01` form matched no pattern, which is the other 2. Split into `marker()`/`isTelevision()` for type and `parse()` for filing — filing behaviour deliberately unchanged, because everything it refuses is a file that would otherwise be moved somewhere wrong. All 48 specials also shared the bare title "The Simpsons"; they now carry their own codes. **Existing rows are not fixed by a rescan** — the scanner skips files it has seen — so `library:reclassify` repairs them: reports by default, `--apply` writes. Dry run against the real library found exactly those 50 and left the 109 real films alone. **Not applied** — it writes to the only copy of the catalogue

title: A failed catalogue download poisoned its own filename, and every later transfer failed identically
description: `41785fc` — `fopen(transfer-incoming.sqlite.gz): Permission denied`, on a transfer that had not contacted the source. The archive was unlinked while the response still held the sink open, which on Windows leaves the *name* in a delete-pending state until the holding process exits — and the queue worker is long-running. Reproduced directly on this machine: open a handle, unlink, reopen, and the reopen fails with exactly that message; close the handle and it succeeds. Fixed twice over — the sink is closed before the archive is touched, and the archive is named per transfer so one poisoned name cannot block another

The dedicated Search tab is removed; `SearchView` became the reusable `SearchResultsList`. Home stopped floating the avatar over the hero. (0.4.0 "Interlude".)

New client API: `updatePlaylist` (PATCH), `reorderPlaylist` (PUT order), `uploadPlaylistCover` (multipart); `Playlist`/`PlaylistDetail` gain `artworkUrl`/`duration_ms`. Server side is S-149 (PR #75). Cover fallback draws a 2×2 track-art mosaic. (0.4.0 "Interlude".)

Server `POST /api/v1/profiles` now returns `color`/`initial`/`avatar_url`.

title: Fix "no audio" playback
description: 2026-09-17 — The stream URL carried the token as a query param, which Sanctum ignores → every stream 401'd (playback started, no audio). Now the bearer token is attached to the AVURLAsset as an Authorization header (survives range requests / seeks).

title: Library "server couldn't load"

title: Now-playing full-screen page
description: 2026-09-17 — Tap the bar → full-screen player: large artwork, working scrubber, transport, and an "Up next" queue.

title: Queue, swipe & kebab actions

title: Settings + profile switch access
description: 2026-09-17 — Account button on Home → Settings: server address, Switch profile, Sign out.

title: Profile switch without sign-out

Server `GET /profiles/mine` + `POST /profiles/switch` issue a fresh profile token from the current one (PIN only where locked); the signed-in view is keyed on an identity generation so it reloads for the new profile.

title: Downloads + offline playback
description: 2026-09-17 — `DownloadStore`: background URLSession downloads a track's stream to disk (self-describing JSON sidecars, excluded from backup); the player prefers the local file for any stored track, so downloads play offline. Download button (progress ring → green check), kebab Download/Remove, and a Downloads screen (Settings → Library) that plays the whole list.

title: Background downloads
description: 2026-09-17 — Background `URLSession` keeps a transfer going while suspended and reattaches on launch. (Partial-file resume is IOS-06b.)

title: Offline: "download all" + delta sync
description: 2026-09-17 — **Download all**: a batch download on an album (and reusable for the whole library) via `DownloadStore.downloadAll`, gated on free space (1 GB floor using `volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage`), skipping already-stored tracks; reports back started/insufficient-space/nothing-to-do. **Delta sync** (was IOS-12): after the first full fetch, launches send the server's last `synced_at` to `POST /api/v1/library/delta` with the held ids, merge only changed items and drop `removed_ids` (deletions + tightened rating caps), and advance the baseline — no full re-fetch each launch. Falls back to a full fetch on a 422 baseline. Baseline cleared with the cache on sign-out/change-server.

title: Shuffle + repeat
description: 2026-09-17 — Shuffle and repeat (off/all/one) in the player and now-playing controls; "Shuffle" on an album plays it shuffled. (Folded into IOS-NPC's now-playing controls.)

title: Playlists
description: 2026-09-17 — Add-to-playlist from the kebab and the left swipe → a sheet that picks an existing playlist or creates one. A Playlists screen (Settings → Library) lists them and plays a playlist's tracks as a queue. New server API: `auth:sanctum` `GET/POST /playlists`, `GET/DELETE /playlists/{id}`, `POST/DELETE /playlists/{id}/items` (account-scoped Collections, gated per track).

title: Admin dashboard
description: 2026-09-17 — Read-only admin dashboard (Settings → Admin, shown only for an admin profile): library counts, activity (plays/accounts/profiles), most-played. Server `GET /api/v1/admin/stats` behind `EnsureApiAdmin`; `/me` returns `is_admin`.

title: Admin: item edit, profiles, scan
description: 2026-09-17 — Completes the admin panel. **Item edit** from a song's ⋯ menu (admin only): title, per-type metadata (artist/album/year, director, episode/season, author/publisher), rating, notes. **Profile management** (Settings → Admin → Profiles): list/add/edit (name, kids, rating cap, PIN)/delete. **Scan for new media** button queues a library scan. Server `GET/PATCH /admin/items/{id}`, `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/profiles`, `POST /admin/scan`.

title: Detail screens

Movies/Shows/Books poster → detail (artwork + play; shows list episodes grouped by season). All derived client-side from the loaded library (album/artist grouping, `children(of:)` in LibraryStore) — no new API.

title: Artwork caching
description: 2026-09-17 — Covers load through a disk-backed URLCache (32MB mem / 512MB disk) via `CachedImage`, so a cover seen once loads instantly and works offline — `AsyncImage` kept nothing and re-fetched on every scroll.

title: Offline: full catalogue browse
description: 2026-09-17 — `/api/v1/library` is cached to disk (`library.json`); a launch shows it instantly and the *whole* catalogue browses offline, not just downloads. Refreshes from the network in the background; the cache is cleared on sign-out/change-server.
